run_text:
Scope: recovery-integrity audit of the quarantine/restore/trash subsystem in the supplied snapshot (uncommitted working tree at HEAD 77be0ec; subsystem absent at HEAD, see git show HEAD:delete_duplicates_gui.py). Reproduction script: .saipen/evidence/recovery-integrity/repro.py, run headless with temp dirs, no real Recycle Bin touched.

IMP-001 [P1] [LOGIC_ERROR] [reproduced] [fix]
expected: durable recovery metadata preserves the immutable identity of an acquired quarantine object (size, SHA-256 fingerprint) across every status transition, because a receipt that loses the identity it vouches for cannot authorize or verify any later recovery
expected-bounded: metadata always carries size and fingerprint, or a transition that cannot supply them is refused rather than written
actual: record_quarantine_metadata() builds a fresh record dict and assigns it wholesale over the stored entry, so any status transition called without size/fingerprint erases them
actual-bounded: logic holds for the initial acquired write; every later write at call sites for statuses trashing, deleted, recycled, restored and restore_refused_occupied passes no size or fingerprint
evidence: delete_duplicates_gui.py:187-196 record dict built with size/fingerprint params defaulting to None; :207 items[abs(qpath)] = record overwrites wholesale; callers delete_duplicates_gui.py:278, 295, 299, 350, 355, 360 all omit size/fingerprint; repro.py D1: fingerprint 'f'*64 and size 7 present after acquired write, both None after trashing write (REPRODUCED)

IMP-002 [P1] [LOGIC_ERROR] [reproduced] [fix]
expected: restore_quarantined_file() with an engine provided refuses any quarantine object whose content cannot be verified against recorded metadata, and a missing fingerprint in the metadata is itself a refusal, never a bypass of verification
expected-bounded: restore with engine but no recorded fingerprint returns a fingerprint_missing-style refusal
actual: the verification guard requires meta.get('fingerprint') to be truthy, so when recovery metadata has no fingerprint (exactly the state IMP-001 produces, or metadata lost/corrupted) the fingerprint check is skipped entirely and the object is renamed into the original path
actual-bounded: logic holds for the normal path with intact metadata; the bypass needs missing fingerprint plus engine passed
evidence: delete_duplicates_gui.py:269 'if engine and meta and meta.get("fingerprint")' gates the whole verify block; :277 os.rename(qpath, dest) runs unverified; repro.py D2: object tampered to 'TAMPERED-DIFFERENT-CONTENT', metadata written with fingerprint=None, restore with engine returned (True, path) and restored the tampered bytes (REPRODUCED)

IMP-003 [P1] [LOGIC_ERROR] [reproduced] [fix]
expected: a durable recovery receipt is written and confirmed before any destructive step; a metadata persistence failure aborts the destructive operation and surfaces to the caller, because os.remove / Recycle Bin cannot be undone when no receipt exists
expected-bounded: record_quarantine_metadata returns success/failure and send_to_trash refuses to destroy on failure
actual: record_quarantine_metadata() swallows OSError with 'except OSError: pass' and returns None, and send_to_trash() ignores the write outcome and proceeds to os.remove / _windows_send_to_recycle_bin with no durable recovery receipt
actual-bounded: logic holds when the journal is writable; the silent loss needs an unwritable RECOVERY_LOG_FILE (directory in the way, full disk, permissions)
evidence: delete_duplicates_gui.py:213-214 'except OSError: pass' with no return value; :348-356 send_to_trash records status but never checks the result before os.remove; repro.py D3: record returned None against an unwritable journal path and send_to_trash destroyed the file anyway (REPRODUCED)

IMP-004 [P1] [LOGIC_ERROR] [reproduced] [fix]
expected: recovery records live in a stable per-user application storage location, discoverable by any later process regardless of its working directory, because the recovery promise must survive the session that created it
expected-bounded: RECOVERY_LOG_FILE resolves to an absolute per-user path (e.g. under the platform per-user application-data directory)
actual: RECOVERY_LOG_FILE = 'quarantine_recovery.json' is relative to the process working directory, so every read and write lands in whatever CWD the app was launched from, and a CWD change makes the records undiscoverable
actual-bounded: logic holds for a single-session, fixed-CWD flow; any later process or a CWD change loses the journal
evidence: delete_duplicates_gui.py:177 RECOVERY_LOG_FILE = 'quarantine_recovery.json'; repro.py D4: after record_quarantine_metadata from one CWD, get_quarantine_metadata from another CWD returns None (REPRODUCED); the value is never normalized to an absolute per-user path anywhere in the module
